primitives.name: Kelly Stake Fraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Skeptic models Reality as Bernoulli(p̂_n) and sets the Kelly-optimal fraction ν_n = M_n/K_{n-1} maximizing E_{p̂_n}[log(1+ν(x_n-p_n))] → ν_n = (p̂_n - p_n)/(p_n(1-p_n)); capital becomes a likelihood ratio K_n = ∏ p̂_i^{x_i}(1-p̂_i)^{1-x_i} / ∏ p_i^{x_i}(1-p_i)^{1-x_i}.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ν_n': 'dimensionless stake fraction', 'p_n': 'probability of event (0 < p_n < 1)', 'p̂_n': "Skeptic's belief about probability (0 < p̂_n < 1)"}
primitives.assumptions: Reality follows Bernoulli distribution; Skeptic uses Kelly criterion for optimal growth rate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p_n approaches 0 or 1, ν_n diverges unless capped.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to compute dynamic bet sizing based on belief discrepancy between forecast and Skeptic's updated estimate.

primitives.name: Logistic Bias Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Logistic model: log(p̂_n/(1-p̂_n)) = log(p_n/(1-p_n)) + θ'c_n, i.e., Skeptic's edge is a logistic correction to the announced log-odds.

primitives.assumptions: Linear relationship in log-odds space; θ captures systematic deviation from forecaster.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Nonlinearities in real-world markets may invalidate linear assumption.

primitives.name: Capital Growth Process
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Game protocol (BPFSI): Forecaster announces p_n ∈ (0,1) and side info c_n ∈ R^d; Skeptic stakes M_n (possibly negative); Reality reveals x_n ∈ {0,1}; capital K_n = K_{n-1} + M_n(x_n - p_n), K_n ≥ 0 (collateral duty).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K_n': 'capital at time n (positive real)', 'M_n': 'stake at time n (real)', 'x_n': 'outcome (0 or 1)', 'p_n': 'announced probability (0 < p_n < 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Skeptic maintains non-negative capital; outcome is binary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Capital may go negative if M_n exceeds K_{n-1} and x_n is unfavorable.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to simulate and track cumulative wealth evolution under varying betting strategies.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of the Bayesian logistic betting strategy hinges on two key components: the Kelly stake fraction and the logistic bias correction. The Kelly fraction ν_n = (p̂_n - p_n)/(p_n(1-p_n)) determines how much of the current bankroll to wager based on the discrepancy between the Skeptic’s belief p̂_n and the Forecaster’s probability p_n. This ensures exponential growth of capital when p̂_n > p_n, assuming the Skeptic's belief is more accurate. The logistic correction log(p̂_n/(1-p̂_n)) = log(p_n/(1-p_n)) + θ'c_n allows the Skeptic to incorporate side information c_n into their belief update, effectively adjusting p_n towards a more accurate p̂_n. These two primitives together define a dynamic betting system that exploits miscalibration in forecasts. The capital process K_n = K_{n-1} + M_n(x_n - p_n) governs wealth evolution, ensuring that gains are made when outcomes align with favorable bets and losses occur otherwise. The theoretical foundation lies in the weak forcing of the strong law of large numbers (SLLN), which guarantees that over time, any consistently miscalibrated forecaster will be bankrupted. However, practical limitations include clipping extreme probabilities, potential overfitting of θ, and finite-sample behavior not captured by asymptotic theorems.
